blocks.text: 1. Real-Time News Assistant
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213195-33291628.png

Healthcare Assistant closed by emphasizing that actual diagnosis or treatment decisions always require a real professional. Real-Time News Assistant, a RAG system design for answering questions from rapidly changing, time-sensitive information, shifts the central design concern from precision to sheer freshness.
It prioritizes freshness of the retrieved index over almost every other design concern.
2. The Design Problem's Scope
Unlike a legal or healthcare knowledge base that changes slowly, news content can go stale within minutes.
An answer that was correct an hour ago can already be wrong now.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Domain","Typical rate of change"],"rows":[["Legal or healthcare content","Slow, changes over weeks or months"],["News content","Can go stale within minutes"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Continuous Real-Time Indexing Pipeline
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213196-718062557.png
Building on real-time updates covered in Real-Time Updates, new articles must be embedded and indexed within seconds or minutes of publication, not batched overnight.
The ingestion pipeline itself runs continuously, never in discrete scheduled batches.
4. Time Decay Weighting In Retrieval
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213196-766907034.png
Much as discounted gain penalizes deep position in NDCG, two articles about the same topic should not rank equally if one is hours old and the other is days old.
Retrieval scoring factors in recency, not just semantic similarity alone.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Article age","Relative retrieval weight"],"rows":[["Recently published","Weighted higher for time-sensitive queries"],["Days or weeks old","Weighted lower, even if semantically similar"]]}

blocks.text: 5. Timestamping Every Answer Explicitly
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213196-643446784.png
Similar to citing page numbers in the generated answer, covered in Chat with PDFs, a generated answer must state when the underlying information was actually published.
A user can judge for themselves whether the answer is still likely current.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: An answer stating 'according to an article published two hours ago' lets the reader judge freshness for themselves, the same transparency as citing page numbers in a generated answer.

blocks.text: 6. Avoiding Overconfident Claims About Developing Events

blocks.alt: Avoiding Overconfident Claims About Developing Events
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213541-344669488.png
As Faithfulness establishes, faithfulness does not check factual accuracy, and a developing story can have facts that later turn out to be wrong or incomplete.
The system prompt should hedge on rapidly evolving stories rather than stating them with excess certainty.
7. Cache Invalidation Must Be Aggressive
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213542-840690752.png
As with time to live as a simple invalidation strategy covered in Response Cache, a response cache with a long time to live is actively harmful in this domain.
Time to live must be set extremely short, or caching should be skipped for time-sensitive queries entirely.
8. High Volume Ingestion Requires Scalable Infrastructure
As Scaling Strategies covers with horizontal versus vertical scaling, a constant stream of new articles from many sources requires ingestion infrastructure that scales independently.
The ingestion pipeline needs its own dedicated scaling plan, distinct from query serving.
9. Recognizing When This Real-Time News Assistant Design Fits The Actual Need

blocks.alt: Recognizing When This Real-Time News Assistant Design Fits The Actual Need
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448213543-925977395.png
A domain where information changes by the minute fits this design.
A stable, slowly changing knowledge base does not need this level of freshness engineering.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Batching ingestion overnight instead of indexing new articles within minutes of publication.
Ranking retrieved articles by semantic similarity alone, ignoring how recent each one actually is.
Omitting a publication timestamp from the generated answer, leaving freshness unclear to the user.
Using a long response cache time to live in a domain where facts change within minutes.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: A real-time news assistant prioritizes freshness of the index above almost every other concern.
News content can go stale within minutes, unlike slower-changing legal or healthcare knowledge bases.
A continuous ingestion pipeline indexes new articles within seconds or minutes, not in overnight batches.
Retrieval scoring should factor in recency, not just semantic similarity, ranking newer content higher.
Every generated answer should explicitly state when the underlying information was published.
The system should hedge on rapidly developing stories rather than stating them with excess certainty.
Response cache time to live must be set extremely short, or skipped for time-sensitive queries entirely.
The ingestion pipeline needs its own dedicated, independently scaling infrastructure.
